findings.description: F001 says the listed guarded commands are the complete plan-mutating surface, but F002 and F003 also add plan worktree create/remove behavior under the plan namespace. The contract separates guard, cleanup, and create rules, so the plan should explicitly classify those subcommands instead of relying on a contradictory completeness claim.

F002 requires gitignored content to block removal and be reported, but the enumerated tests do not pin an ignored-content refusal fixture. This is central to the preservation outcome and could regress while still satisfying the listed dirty and untracked tests.

F003 pins missing-config notices by default and divergent refusal during opt-in copy, but it does not clearly require default create-time detection and reporting of an already-present divergent allowlisted file. The objective says missing and divergent operator-local config must be declared explicitly.

The completion test requires fixture tests with zero live auditor calls, but F001 does not explicitly pin auditor stubbing or no-network assertions for audit and orchestrate dispatch entry-point tests. Those commands are the most likely to accidentally cross into live auditor behavior.

Override behavior is not pinned per refusal class. F001 clearly fail-closes corrupt registry loads, but also says an explicit override proceeds after evidence, leaving ambiguity over whether wrong path, unhealthy binding, swapped repo, indeterminate git state, and corrupt registry are all overrideable or whether some are absolute stops.

F002 does not specify or test what happens if registry binding deletion fails after the audit entry is flushed and after git worktree removal starts or succeeds. That leaves a cleanup path where the worktree can be gone but the registry still records a binding, which undermines the clean_removed_audited outcome.

The journey state names divergent_refused, but F003 says default create only detects and reports divergent allowlisted files, reserving refusal for copy-time overwrite attempts. The intended user-facing result for no-flag divergence is therefore ambiguous.

F001 declares the listed guarded commands to be the complete plan-mutating surface, but F002 and F003 introduce or modify plan worktree remove and plan worktree create, both of which mutate registry or worktree state. The plan needs an explicit decision that these commands are exempt from the wrong-worktree guard, or they need equivalent guard coverage.

F002 requires audit-first deletion, but the described audit record appears to encode a successful removal before the destructive git worktree remove step has actually succeeded. The registry-only completion path then relies on an audit log entry for successful removal, which can be ambiguous after partial failures.

F003 asserts that no symlinks are created in the new worktree, but it does not pin behavior when an allowlisted source file or preexisting target path is itself a symlink. That leaves a deterministic-rule gap for the no-symlinks-in-v1 policy and for copy-time overwrite refusal.
F001 requires override evidence to be durably written but only pins this as flushed, leaving the crash-durability contract ambiguous for the override record and binding snapshot.
F002 blocks unregistered nested .git directories but does not pin the policy for registered submodules containing dirty, untracked, or ignored local state that git worktree removal may still delete.
F002 specifies a post-destruction removal-OUTCOME audit entry but does not pin behavior if that outcome append fails after git worktree remove succeeds.
F003 says the initial allowlist entry is environments_json, but the contract needs an exact repo-root-relative path so tests and implementation cannot diverge on the local config file name.

F002 states removal is eligible only when the binding passes binding_health, but later requires a registry-only completion path when the worktree path no longer exists after a prior audited removal intent. A missing worktree should fail binding_health, so the precedence between fail-closed health gating and registry-only completion is contradictory.

F003 says the initial allowlist entry is the repo-root-relative path environments_json while also saying it is the file named environments.json and that the exact string is pinned. That ambiguity can make implementation and tests disagree on the actual allowlisted path.

F001 requires an override flag with a required reason and says refusals name the exact override command, but the CLI spelling and reason argument shape are not pinned. The user-facing override journey needs deterministic command text and tests that prove the intended surface.

F002 specifies an important post-destruction failure mode where the worktree removal succeeds but the OUTCOME audit append fails, requiring a non-zero exit that says removal succeeded but outcome recording failed. The listed tests do not explicitly cover that behavior.

F002 adds safety rules for nested .git directories and registered submodules, including ignored-content preservation recursively, but the named test list does not include fixtures for those cases. Those rules protect the same local-state preservation outcome as ignored files in the parent worktree.

F002 has an ordering ambiguity: it says the removal-OUTCOME entry is appended after destructive steps finish, but later says only then does it run git worktree remove and delete the registry binding. That leaves the audit/removal/registry mutation sequence underdetermined.

F002 introduces a registry-only completion path after a prior audited intent, but the acceptance text only says it is itself audited. It does not pin whether that completion audit must be written before deleting the stale registry entry or how unwritable audit storage behaves on this path.

F003 pins behavior when an allowlisted source file exists in repo_root, but it does not specify the source-absent matrix for environments.json. If the base checkout lacks the allowlisted file, create-time notices and --copy-local-config behavior could silently no-op.

The contract's non-goals say there should be no changes to v0 registry/create/visibility surfaces, but F003 adds default create-time notices and a new --copy-local-config option on plan worktree create. That may be the intended exception, but the plan does not explicitly reconcile the conflict before implementation.

F003 pins behavior when an allowlisted file exists in repo_root but is missing or divergent in the new worktree, but it does not pin the source-missing cases: absent in repo_root, absent in both places, or absent in repo_root but already present in the target.

F002's registry-only completion path for a missing worktree with a prior removal-INTENT bypasses the normal Step 7 wording. It says to append a completion OUTCOME and exit, but does not explicitly pin fsync requirements or the failure behavior if that outcome write fails after the registry entry is deleted.

F001 says worktree create is outside the wrong-worktree guard but protected by strict registry loading, while F003's create acceptance tests focus only on local config behavior. There is no explicit create-path test that a corrupt registry refuses before any filesystem creation or local-config copy occurs.

F001 pins durable override evidence in prose, but the proposed tests collapse the failure mode to a generic write-failure test. That does not prove independent write, flush, and fsync failures for the override record versus the binding snapshot all refuse before the guarded command executes.

F002 requires append AND fsync for removal intent and outcome entries, but the proposed tests name unwritable intent log and outcome append failure only. Fsync failure before physical removal is materially different and must be proven to refuse with the worktree untouched.

F002 says a git worktree remove failure appends an OUTCOME entry, but it does not pin what happens if that failure-outcome append or fsync itself fails. The step-level contract promises each failure arm is pinned, so this audit reporting failure path remains underspecified.

F002's cleanup policy covers registered submodules with modified, staged, untracked, or gitignored content, but the proposed test list only names a dirty-submodule refusal. That leaves the recursive preservation rule underpinned for ignored and untracked submodule content.

F001 places worktree create outside the wrong-worktree guard, while F003 defines local-config comparison against repo_root without pinning which checkout supplies that source when create is invoked from an existing worktree or symlinked path. That leaves missing/divergent notices and opt-in copies dependent on invocation context.

F001 states that override requires a reason, but the proposed acceptance tests do not explicitly pin absent, empty, or whitespace-only reason refusal. Without that matrix cell, the durable evidence path could accept non-substantive override evidence.

reason: Operator-directed (D010 follow-through): after the F002 numbered-algorithm restructure, round 7 returned zero ordering/policy findings; the remaining high is implementation_detail — a create-path test pin whose substance ALREADY ships tested in v0 (test_worktrees_registry.py TestCreate corrupt-registry refusal precedes all filesystem work because strict load is create's first step); the residual ask (assert refusal also precedes the new local-config copy) is a trivially-added implementation test the post-impl audit will check. Three medium prose pins resolved via recorded dispositions. Seven rounds, 100% clearance every round, policy undisputed since D003.
